study: Closing-auction imbalance, stage 1 (small paid historical sample): when Nasdaq's pre-close imbalance messages show a large one-sided BUY imbalance, does buying at the ask a few seconds later and selling in the closing cross beat the same-moment names without such an imbalance, by >= +5 bp and net of cost?
registered_at: 2026-10-22, before any data is priced or downloaded
origin: Operator 10/22 asked for a separate idea that can reach the +5 to +11 bp bar. Forced flows are the one family with a structural reason to move prices (month-end rebalancing +20.6 bp, t 3.7 over 289 months). The closing auction concentrates index, ETF and fund flows; Nasdaq publishes the Net Order Imbalance Indicator (NOII) before the close. Untested here.
prior: LOW-MODERATE (~10-15%). The effect is documented in market-microstructure research, but it is widely traded; the after-cost size for a retail account entering on the public message is the open question. Index adds/deletes were priced at the announcement (10/2); this is the daily, smaller cousin.
stage: STAGE 1 only: a small historical sample to decide whether any money (live imbalance data, more history) is worth spending. A stage-1 PASS buys nothing by itself: it earns a stage-2 prereg (larger sample, NYSE names, live data cost).

data.source: Databento XNAS.ITCH, schema 'imbalance' (Nasdaq NOII: paired shares, imbalance shares and side, reference / near / far prices), Nasdaq-listed common stock only, against the remaining Databento new-account credit (about $118 after 10/4).
data.sample: 40 sessions drawn by seed sha256('closing-imbalance-stage1') from 2026-05-11 .. 2026-10-15 (the warehouse window, so SIP bars and the liquid universe are on hand), 20 per half (halves at 2026-07-29); names = warehouse liquid names (>= $10, 20-day $20M ADV) that are Nasdaq-listed (listing exchange from Alpaca assets).
data.budget_guard: Price the full request list with Databento metadata.get_cost before any download; abort if > $25 (then shrink sessions, never per-name sampling, and re-price). Spend is logged per request.
data.quotes_and_close: SIP NBBO quotes around the decision time and the official closing cross price from Alpaca historical (free, data-only account).

signal.decision_time: T = 15:50:00 ET, the first NOII publication (or the session's first imbalance message at or after 15:50:00 for that name, within 5 s; else no signal).
signal.size: IMB = imbalance shares x reference price / the name's 20-day mean daily dollar volume (prior sessions, from warehouse daily data).
signal.buy_side: BUY = imbalance side is buy AND IMB is in the top decile of all names' IMB at T in that half (cut computed on half A, applied to both halves, outcome-blind).

trade: Entry: the SIP ask of the last clean quote at or before T + 5 s (<= 5 s old; else dropped and counted). Exit: the official closing cross price (an MOC sell in a real account; paper accounts do not run auctions, so this is the price a real account gets). Net = close / entry ask - 1 (the entry half-spread is inside; the auction exit has no spread). Gross = close / entry mid - 1.
control: The REST: every other in-universe Nasdaq name at the same T in the same session (no buy imbalance in the top decile), scored identically. Information: a same-name control on a random other session in the same half without a top-decile buy imbalance.
statistic: Per session: mean gross of BUY names minus mean gross of the rest (sessions with >= 3 BUY names), session-equal, session-clustered t (df = sessions - 1); halves as above.
power: Outcome-blind count step after the imbalance data is downloaded and before any close or quote is read: BUY counts per half and sessions with >= 3 BUY names; projected MDE from the rest's session-level SD of a placebo window (15:40:05 -> 15:50:00 gross, before the signal; not the outcome). Floors: >= 300 BUY entries and >= 15 sessions per half, else UNDERPOWERED.
pass: In BOTH halves: BUY - rest >= +5 bp gross with t >= 2.0; BUY mean NET > 0; dropping the 3 sessions and (separately) the 3 names with the largest share keeps the difference >= 0. FAIL: t <= -2 in a half, or the 97.5% upper bound < +5 bp in both halves. Otherwise UNDERPOWERED.
information_only: SELL-side top decile (would a short-into-the-close pay; the desk is long-only)
IMB terciles and the imbalance's change 15:50 -> 15:55
the near / far price vs the last trade as a fair-value read
live_feasibility: Declared up front: trading this live needs real-time imbalance data (not in Alpaca's feed; Databento live or a Nasdaq feed, paid) and a real account for MOC exits. Stage 2 must price that before any test that could lead to it.
no_retuning: 15:50, top decile, the 20-day ADV scale, T + 5 s, the sample seed and size, the halves and the bars are fixed.

amended: 2026-10-22, before any data, after result-skeptic FIX FIRST (items 2-8; item 1 is the status above). (2) ADV = the mean of 20 prior sessions' RAW SIP daily-bar dollar volume (Alpaca historical; daily.pkl holds no volume and warehouse minute bars omit the closing print). (3) CONTROL = in-universe Nasdaq names at T with NEITHER a top-decile buy NOR a top-decile sell imbalance. (4) The decile cut is on SIGNED IMB (buy positive), the 90th percentile of half A's pooled values across all its sessions, applied unchanged to both halves. (5) The closing price is the Nasdaq official closing-cross print in Alpaca SIP trades (its tape-C condition code verified from the data); no print = the name-day is dropped; the daily-bar close is not used unless 5 name-days are hand-checked equal to that print. (6) Before any outcome is read, the data must confirm: close-auction messages only (auction-type filter), the NOII cadence after 15:50, the first-message time, and the field mapping (paired, imbalance, side, reference / near / far prices); any mismatch is an amendment before scoring. (7) The projected MDE uses the 15:50:05 -> close gross on sessions OUTSIDE the sample (free SIP), not a 15:40-15:50 window. (8) Russell reconstitution, quad-witching (third Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec) and MSCI rebalance days are flagged; results are reported with and without them (the verdict uses all days). NOTES: Nasdaq-listed is taken from the NOII data itself (symbology mapped, e.g. share classes); SEC/TAF fees (~0.3 bp) are charged on the exit; with 20 sessions a half the MDE may be ~7 bp - the count step decides; live use needs paid real-time imbalance data and a real account, which stage 2 must price against 'no spend until proven'.

amended_3.when: 2026-10-22, before any download, after result-skeptic code FIX FIRST (11 items).
changes: (1) CLOSE = the Nasdaq closing cross: SIP trades in 16:00:00-16:05:00 from exchange 'Q' only; primary = the largest size-carrying '6' print from Q; Q's 'M' print is a cross-check (disagreements counted and printed); no Q '6' print = no close (counted).

(2) Before scoring, --closecheck dumps (exchange, conditions, size, price) of every candidate print for 30 names on the first session; --score refuses until that dump is reviewed and recorded (--confirm closecheck).

(3) --extract refuses until probe.json records a mapping confirmation (--confirm probe); it aborts if a session has no auction_type 'C' or a side outside {B, A, N}; non-finite ref / imbalance values are dropped and counted.
(4) The probe window is 15:49:30-15:50:10 so the first closing-message time is visible.
(5) Paid downloads are not retried; every attempt is logged against the $25 cap before it is made.

(6) MDE (amended (7)) on warehouse sessions OUTSIDE the sample in the window, Nasdaq-listed names only, entry = the 15:50 SIP bar open, exit = the closing cross from (1) (Alpaca, free), k = the half's median BUY count, n = the half's projected sessions with >= 3 BUY names.
(7) The 40 sessions are frozen here (none is a flagged day); the script refuses a different draw.
(8) The count step reports requested names, names with any closing message, names with one at T, and requested names with none (possible symbol mismatches).
(9) Drops counted separately: no quote at T + 5 s, no closing cross, symbol missing from the Alpaca response.
(10) Drop-3 sessions = drop the 3 largest session differences (session-equal).

(11) Information implemented: BUY lift by IMB tercile (within BUY); by the 15:50 -> 15:55 change of signed IMB (up vs down); entry at T + 30 s (ask <= 5 s old); same-name control (the name's BUY gross minus its mean gross on other sample sessions of the half where it is CTRL). Amended out: the 15:55 decision (Nasdaq's MOC entry cutoff is 15:55, untradeable as an MOC exit) and near / far prices (fields not confirmed; any later read is post-hoc).
